description: Chains, membership, the fork rule, cuts, content records and checkpoints end to end (sections 4.4, 5, 6, 9).

vectors.name: group/lifecycle-roles
vectors.description: Genesis, a writer, a reader. A reader's record and a stranger's are ignored. Carol's first record names a mhead from when she was a reader and stays ignored after she is promoted; her second, written after the promotion, is accepted (draft 2 judges the author as of mhead; draft 1 said "at some point in its epoch").

vectors.name: group/remove-with-cut-unlisted-device-and-new-epoch
vectors.description: Bob writes twice on device b1 and once on device b2, then is removed with a cut that lists only (b1, seq 1); an epoch record follows. His b1 seq 1 is accepted. His b1 seq 2 and 3 (beyond the cut) and every record on devices b2 and b3 (chains the cut does not list, including one from a device nobody had seen) are ignored when sealed in epoch 0. A record sealed in epoch 1 is ignored because he is not a writer as of its mhead.

vectors.name: group/waiting-for-new-key-after-removal
vectors.description: A removal with no epoch record after it: the group is waiting for a new key, so devices MUST NOT seal content records (may_seal_content false). A content record sealed anyway, under the old epoch with the removal as mhead, is accepted by this implementation: the specification gives a reader no rule against it (finding).

vectors.name: group/new-key-after-removal
vectors.description: The same group once the epoch record has arrived: no longer waiting.

vectors.name: group/waiting-for-new-key-after-replacement
vectors.description: A replacement (kind 4) also leaves the group waiting for a new key until an epoch record follows.

vectors.name: group/lower-writer-then-raise-needs-new-epoch
vectors.description: A writer is lowered to reader with a cut, which needs no new epoch: a record beyond the cut (written with the old mhead) and one written as a reader are both ignored. Raising him again in the same epoch is invalid (6.2) and is ignored; after an epoch record the same raise is valid, and his record sealed in epoch 1 is accepted.

vectors.name: group/invalid-membership-records
vectors.description: Records that name the current head as mprev and are each invalid for a different reason (reasons in `ignored`); they are kept and ignored, and the one valid add continues the chain.

vectors.name: group/fork-1-epoch-record-after-removal
vectors.description: bob removes dave; bob writes the epoch record; carol concurrently adds erin with the removal as mprev. carol has the smaller pid, but step 1 of 6.5 makes the epoch record by the author of the removal win. The group is no longer waiting.

vectors.name: group/fork-1-epoch-record-by-another-manager
vectors.description: carol removes dave. bob writes the epoch record, carol (the author of the removal) adds erin. Step 1 needs an epoch record by the author of the removal, so it does not apply; no one is dropped (step 2); step 3 picks the smaller author, carol, so the addition wins and the group is left waiting for a new key.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-author-removed-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob removes carol. carol has the smaller pid and would win step 3, but step 2 drops the candidate whose author is removed by another candidate, so the removal wins.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-author-lowered-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob lowers carol to reader. Lowering counts like removal in step 2 (no epoch is needed for it).

vectors.name: group/fork-2-author-replaced-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob replaces carol's secret. A replacement counts like a removal in step 2.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-mutual-removal-keeps-all
vectors.description: Each of carol and bob removes the other at the same mprev. Step 2 would drop both, so it keeps both and step 3 picks the smaller author: carol's removal of bob wins.

vectors.name: group/fork-3-least-author
vectors.description: carol and bob add different people at the same mprev; neither removes the other, so the smaller author (carol) wins. The loser and the record that follows it on its branch are ignored (lost_fork, off_chain).

vectors.name: group/fork-3-same-author-two-devices
vectors.description: One manager writes two different additions from two devices at the same mprev (two chains, so neither is a chain fork). The tuple (author, device, seq, record_id) is compared element by element: the smaller device_id wins.

vectors.name: group/fork-three-candidates
vectors.description: Three managers at the same mprev. bob removes carol; carol adds erin; alice adds frank. Step 2 drops carol's candidate (its author is removed by another), leaving bob's removal and alice's addition; step 3 picks the smaller author, alice. Without step 2 carol's would have won.

vectors.name: group/fork-three-candidates-cycle
vectors.description: carol removes alice, alice removes bob, bob removes carol, all at the same mprev. Every candidate's author is removed by another, so step 2 drops them all and keeps them all; step 3 picks the smallest author, carol.

vectors.name: group/content-mhead-on-losing-branch
vectors.description: Two additions fork at one mprev; carol's wins. Erin's record names the winner as mhead: accepted. Records that name the losing addition as mhead are ignored, even from a manager (the author writes the change again). Frank is not a member on the winning chain, so a record naming the winner is ignored too. A record whose mhead is not held waits.

vectors.name: group/genesis-duplicates-and-invalid
vectors.description: Two valid genesis records (same creator, nonce and K_0, different device and clock): the one with the smaller record_id is used and the other is ignored as a duplicate (6.1). Three invalid ones are ignored: a nonce that does not give this gid, a card that is not the creator's, and a commitment that does not match K_0.

vectors.name: group/chain-fork
vectors.description: Bob's device b1 has two different records with seq 2. Neither is accepted, nothing later in the chain (seq 3) is accepted, seq 1 is; both are kept and the fork is shown. Alice's other chain is unaffected.

vectors.name: group/chain-duplicate-delivery
vectors.description: The same sealed record delivered twice (identical bytes) is one record.

vectors.name: group/chain-same-body-sealed-twice
vectors.description: A device seals the same change (same body fields) twice with different salts, which a device MUST NOT do (4.4). Section 4.4 calls records with "the same body bytes" one record "whatever their salts", but the body includes the signature, which covers the header and so the salt: two such records never have the same body bytes. This implementation reads "body bytes" literally, so the two are different records with the same seq, a fork (finding).

vectors.name: group/chain-gap-and-prev-mismatch
vectors.description: Bob's b1 chain is missing seq 2 (seq 3 waits: gap). His b2 chain has a seq 2 whose prev is not the record the reader holds as seq 1 (waits: prev_mismatch). Both are "behind", never errors.

vectors.name: group/held-back-exactly-24h
vectors.description: A record exactly 24 hours ahead of the reader's time is accepted, and so is the one after it. The reader's time is BASE_MS + 5000.

vectors.name: group/held-back-one-ms-over
vectors.description: A record 24 hours and 1 ms ahead is held back, and the record after it waits behind it (gap): its chain has a hole until the reader's time catches up. The reader's time is BASE_MS + 5000.

vectors.name: group/held-back-membership-record
vectors.description: A membership record 24 hours and 1 ms ahead is held back, so it is not on the chain; carol's record names it as mhead and waits (mhead_unknown), and bob's, which names the head before it, is accepted.

vectors.name: group/replace-secret-by-the-person-with-cut
vectors.description: Bob replaces his own secret (signed with the old key) with a cut listing (b1, seq 1); alice writes the epoch record. The new pid takes bob's role. Draft 2 gives kind 4 a cut: bob's b1 seq 2, a record on a device the cut does not list, and a late record written with the old key are all ignored (beyond_cut). The new pid's record sealed in epoch 1 is accepted.

vectors.name: group/replace-secret-rules
vectors.description: A replacement naming a pid that is already a member, one written by someone who is neither a manager nor the person, and one for a pid that is not a member are ignored; a manager's replacement is valid.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-full-history
vectors.description: Alice's items, a checkpoint by manager bob that restates the winning writes and covers alice's chain up to seq 5 and his own first record, then later records. All records present: covered content is folded from the checkpoint and the records, the rest on top.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-covered-records-deleted
vectors.description: The same group after the covered content records (alice seq 3 to 5) were deleted from storage. Alice's membership record at seq 6 is accepted only because the checkpoint covers the gap. The current values are unchanged; the history before the checkpoint is gone.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-by-non-manager
vectors.description: A checkpoint written by a writer (not a manager) is ignored and covers nothing.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-purged
vectors.description: A manager's checkpoint names the item and the place of the second write in `purged`: the first two writes of its password are forgotten (no history), the third survives. A reader that still holds the records for the first two drops them from its state too.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-overlapping-order-1
vectors.description: Two checkpoints by two managers overlap: the first covers alice's chain up to q2, the second up to q3 (q2 is in both). Records listed with the first checkpoint first.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-overlapping-order-2
vectors.description: The same records listed with the second checkpoint first (and in reverse): the same result.
